notes: Across all five rungs Claude's library claims hold up against the installed packages. Media-chrome React imports (MediaController, MediaPlayButton, MediaMuteButton, MediaVolumeRange, MediaTimeRange, MediaTimeDisplay, MediaPipButton, MediaFullscreenButton, MediaPosterImage) all match media-chrome 4.19.0's dist/react/index.d.ts, and the MuxVideo default export from @mux/mux-video-react 0.31.0 is valid. Props used on MuxVideo (playbackId, streamType="on-demand", autoPlay, muted, loop, playsInline, crossOrigin, slot) and the showDuration attribute on MediaTimeDisplay are all documented in MuxMediaProps / media-chrome JSDoc. Every authored CSS custom property is real: --media-primary-color, --media-secondary-color, --media-control-background, --media-control-hover-background, --media-font-family, --media-button-icon-width, --media-control-padding and the --media-range-* family are documented in media-chrome-range.d.ts, media-chrome-button.d.ts and media-time-range.d.ts; the three Mux-Player-specific vars used in earlier rungs (--media-accent-color, --controls-backdrop-color, --fullscreen-button) were discovered and validated by Claude through live shadow-DOM inspection of the bundled Gerwig theme CSS before being applied. The vertical-layer and bottom part names referenced via querySelector were taken verbatim from the player's own ::part(...) rules and media-control-bar[part~='bottom'] selectors observed in the rendered shadow DOM. The .media accessor on <mux-player> matches video-api.d.ts (get media(): MuxVideoElement | undefined | null), and the userinactive attribute on media-controller is documented on MediaContainer.
